newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief reshuffles human rights staff.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief reshuffles human rights staff.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Thursday reassigned a key human rights administrator from Geneva to New York in what U.N. sources said was an effort to end feuding in the rights operation.

Ibrahima Fall, the assistant secretary-general for human rights and director of the Centre for Human Rights, will be moved to the Department of Political Affairs in New York, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard announced.

Fall will replace Lansana Kouyate of Guinea, who is also an assistant secretary-general, Eckhard said. Kouyate was expected to go to Zaire and work with Mohammed Sahnoun, the new U.N. envoy to Central Africa.

Fall, a former Senegalese foreign minister and professor of constitutional law, had differences with Jose Ayala Lasso, the High Commissioner for Human Rights, who was appointed as his boss in a job created by the General Assembly in 1994.
The feuding has been widely discussed among human rights groups who said it was hurting the effectiveness of the office.
U.N. officials said privately that the so-called personality clash was only one problem and that the structure of the human rights centre and Ayala Lasso's post needed to be defined more clearly.
Since Annan took office this year, human rights groups have been pressuring him to give a higher priority to the protection from violence and abuse of individuals.

Ayala Lasso, a former U.N. ambassador and international lawyer from Ecuador, has also been criticised by some diplomats and rights groups for his relatively low profile in drawing public attention to abuses.
Fall's successor has not been announced. He was appointed to the director of the centre in August 1992 and made an assistant secretary-general for human rights in December of that year.
